ownership_reason: Only the gold sees one type variable together with the hierarchy of the parent type: hop 3 rebuilds the structure of the field type around its variables and hands each variable on, hop 4 passes it through, hops 1 and 2 never see a variable. The convention is pinned outside the gold: ObjectNavigator.navigateClassFields evaluates the fields of every superclass with the type of the navigated object, so the parent type of an inherited field is the subclass (Bar.class for Foo's fields in the trigger); TypeToken.getSuperclassTypeParameter reads the type argument that a raw subclass assigns through its generic superclass (the TypeToken idiom every TypeToken-based test relies on); TypeToken.isAssignableFrom walks the whole generic superclass chain mapping each class's type parameters to the arguments assigned below it. The gold's javadoc promises the type that the parent type assigns to the variable; Bar assigns String to S through Foo<String, Integer>, and the variant returns S itself. A one-level substitution of the parent type above the gold (rawParentClass.getGenericSuperclass() with getSuperclass() at hop 4, or the same on the parent type at hops 1-3) passes the existing tests but is not consistent with the path: it hands the gold a parent type that is not the type of the object that contains the field (the documented parameter of hops 1-4 and of the gold, and what ObjectNavigator passes), and a variable assigned two levels up (class Baz extends Bar, navigated as Baz.class) stays unassigned, where the correct gold, like TypeToken.isAssignableFrom, climbs any number of levels.
